memory_candidates.content: In the agent-system source store, scripts that resolve their repo root as "$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)" are only correct in a deploy tree (.claude/scripts/ or .opencode/scripts/ — the deploy tree is NOT singular). Run from agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ the same expression silently resolves to agent-system/extensions/ rather than failing. Guard structurally on the grandparent dir name via ${SCRIPT_DIR%/*} parameter expansion (basename(SCRIPT_DIR) is always literally 'scripts' and carries no signal). Never use `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` as the fix: it silently succeeds by finding the true root, masking the invocation error. When sourcing a shared guard helper into these scripts, always write `. "${SCRIPT_DIR}/guard.sh" || exit 1` — several core scripts use `set -uo pipefail` or no `set` at all, so a bare source of a missing helper prints an error but CONTINUES with an unvalidated root. Related: editing any deployed-identical source script flips check-extension-docs.sh Rule F (check_deployed_script_drift, a hard fail) red until a manual <leader>al sync; this is expected and cannot be resolved headlessly.

A single shared sourced guard/helper file (~25 lines) that validates its own BASH_SOURCE[0] location beats N per-caller inline copies when the check is caller-independent: it needs no arguments, is indifferent to each caller's differently-named root variable, and centralizes future edits (e.g. adding a third accepted deploy-tree name) to one file instead of N. Net new code was ~37 lines (helper + 24 one-line callers) vs. ~120 for 24 self-contained inline blocks.
